core.title: Declare the runtime the file executes in
core.given: A non-test implementation file in a project governed by this convention's structure profile, new or existing
core.when: the file is present in the codebase (created, edited, or untouched) and its runtime declaration is checked
core.then: The file MUST carry the profile's runtime declaration with a value from the stack's runtime vocabulary that names where the file actually executes (the server-side value, the client-side value, or, for a module that genuinely executes in both, the both-sides value when the vocabulary provides one).
prefer: During GREEN: derive the value from the real execution path created or used by the current acceptance (where the module is actually loaded and run), not from file location or hypothetical reuse.
During GREEN: keep an existing correct runtime declaration.
During GREEN: change only the declaration header when the implementation already executes in the correct place.
Use the both-sides value only for a module that genuinely runs in both execution environments.
avoid: Broadening the fix: moving code between execution environments merely to fit a preferred label.
Guessing the both-sides value because the file could theoretically run in both places.
Picking a wrong single-side value for a module that really runs in both places.
unless: Files in test roles (unit test, acceptance test, e2e test) are excluded.
core.why: Where a module executes is not evident from its location, and a wrong or missing declaration is inherited by every downstream reader; when the stack's execution model can run one module in more than one environment, the vocabulary must offer a both-sides value, or authors would be forced to pick a wrong single-side one.
evidence: The convention check for this rule reports no finding for the file (findings are evidence and repair triggers, not activation prerequisites).
The declaration matches where the file actually executes (a valid value alone is not sufficient).
The current behavioral acceptance passes in its real runtime.
verification: The check verifies, for every in-scope implementation file, that the runtime declaration is present and that its value belongs to the stack's runtime vocabulary; files in test roles are excluded from detection.

The check does not by itself verify that the declared value matches the file's actual execution path, including genuine dual execution; that needs an execution-path observer, and findings are repair triggers, not activation prerequisites.
A missing declaration is reported at the file's URN binding line, or at the first meaningful line when the file has no URN.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the stack's checker fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: A new implementation file has no runtime declaration line.
An existing implementation file lacks a runtime declaration, even if the current change does not touch its header.
An implementation file's declared value is not one of the stack's allowed runtime values.
An implementation file's declared runtime does not match where it actually executes (e.g. its execution path changed but the declaration was left untouched).
A module genuinely runs in both execution environments and is declared with a single-side value instead of the both-sides value.
doesNotFire: Files in test roles (unit test, acceptance test, e2e test).
Files governed by another stack's structure profile (each stack realizes this obligation with its own vocabulary and check).

profileRequirements.meaning: The header construct by which an implementation file declares the runtime environment it executes in; this is the declaration the core's obligation, prefer and avoid items read and write.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the `Runtime:` header line naming where the file executes

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's closed vocabulary of runtime-declaration values and what each names: the server-side value, the client-side value, and — when the stack's execution model can run one module in both — a both-sides value.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `bun`, `browser`, `isomorphic`; allowed values on Bun, where `isomorphic` means a module that genuinely runs both server-side and in the browser

bunOnly.text: Bun decides at run time what a bundler decides at build time, so a full-stack Bun module can routinely run in both places; without an `isomorphic` value authors would be forced to pick a wrong one and every downstream reader would inherit the error.
bunOnly.reason: The rationale rests on Bun's run-time execution model versus bundler build-time placement and names the Bun vocabulary token; the core keeps only the generic rationale (wrong declarations are inherited; a both-sides value is required when a module can execute in both environments).

bunOnly.text: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-HEADER-001 / BUN-GREEN-HEADER-RUNTIME-001 finding for the file.
bunOnly.reason: Detector, validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details; the core refers to the rule's convention check generically.

bunOnly.text: Per-stack vocabulary: Vite reads `vite|browser|node`, Python reads `python`; `isomorphic` has no Vite counterpart and is the substantive Bun addition.
bunOnly.reason: Cross-stack comparison of other realizations' vocabularies; the neutral core only requires the vocabulary to come from the profile (idiom.source_syntax#runtime_values).

bunOnly.text: Rationale for isomorphic: a bundler stack decides at BUILD time which code reaches the browser, so a file is server or client by where the bundler puts it; Bun decides at RUN time, e.g. a fragment renderer used server-side and again after a client-side swap.
bunOnly.reason: Bun-versus-bundler argumentation with a stack-specific worked example; its neutral content is already carried by core.why.

bunOnly.text: path_glob = <files belonging to a project whose stack is Bun>; stack context must be explicit (repository stack configuration identifying the Bun realization), language (TypeScript/JavaScript) is NOT a proxy since the Vite stack uses the same languages with a different vocabulary; needs an observer that resolves the file's stack from repository configuration.
bunOnly.reason: Stack membership names the Bun realization and is retained here in the realization together with its required stack-resolution observer (language is not a proxy). It is not expressed through a profile key: roots.config documents only the path of the file that declares repository roots and profile choices — a location, not a membership predicate — and bun.json supplies no such configuration path, so no configuration path is invented. The core is scoped instead by binding it to the stack's structure profile (core.given, doesNotFire).

bunOnly.text: Finding ids GREEN-HEADER-001 (shared core alias, also carried by the Python realization and coder.vite.green-header-runtime — one obligation, three per-stack detectors) and BUN-GREEN-HEADER-RUNTIME-001.
bunOnly.reason: Finding ids and cross-realization alias bookkeeping are realization details; the core states the finding kinds generically (missing, invalid vocabulary, mismatch with actual execution).

No neutral fact type exists for stack membership in the closed vocabulary, and no profile key fits: roots.config is only the path of the configuration file that declares repository roots and profile choices — a location, not a membership predicate or resolution procedure — and bun.json supplies no such path, so none is invented. Bun membership and its required stack-resolution observer are retained in the realization (bunOnly); the core is scoped by binding it to the stack's structure profile.

Neutral finding fact: missing declaration, value outside the vocabulary, or mismatch with actual execution (needs an execution-path observer; findings are repair triggers, not prerequisites); the concrete finding ids are bunOnly.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself ('the file says where it runs', and the declaration must match actual execution) is fully neutral. What could not be made neutral: (a) the declaration syntax (`Runtime:` line) and the value vocabulary (`bun`/`browser`/`isomorphic`) are stack data, moved to two proposed idiom keys since the closed vocabulary has no fit; (b) the rationale contrasting run-time with build-time execution is Bun argumentation, kept as bunOnly with a generic rationale in core.why; (c) detector/finding ids and the Vite/Python vocabulary comparison are realization details (bunOnly); (d) stack-membership scoping has no fact type in the closed enum and no fitting profile key — roots.config documents only the path of the file that declares repository roots and profile choices, which is a location rather than a membership predicate, and bun.json supplies no such configuration path, so none is invented — it is therefore retained entirely in the realization: the core is bound to a stack's structure profile, and the Bun-specific membership observer (resolving the file's stack from repository configuration, language not being a proxy) stays bunOnly. Which files count as test roles is supplied by the realizing profile's role assignment — bun.json states only 'test files are excluded'. The URN binding line in the report-location rule is a framework concept (urn group), not a stack one, so it stays in core.verification.
